newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close narrowly lower.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close narrowly lower.

text.p: Argentine stocks clawed back losses late Monday to end just shy of even, although traders expected the tone to remain guarded Tuesday ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve talks.
"The fall was stifled by a lack of volume, which caused prices to bounce back selectively," said Jorge Bonanno at traders Interfin.
The blue-chip MerVal index dipped 0.1 percent to 809.41, recovering from a low of 803.32.

"There's still good support at 800, where sellers vanish," Bonanno said. "Stocks will probably drift between 800-830 until they digest the outcome of this week's Fed meeting and the Mexican elections."
Floor volume shrank to 20.1 million pesos from $35.8 million Friday while over-the-counter turnover was extremely weak at 33.8 million pesos against 87.8 million Friday.

"The market continues to consolidate and the pattern it's following is very healthy," another trader said. "We expect another quiet day tomorrow, and things should start to pick up from Wednesday, maybe with some volatility."
The broad market index also closed off 0.1 percent, with losers beating winners 30 to 17 and 26 stocks closing flat.
MerVal losers were led by pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which dropped 4.1 percent, foods giant Molinos Rio de la Plata, off 3.2 percent, and holding company Comercial del Plata, down 2.4 percent.

Best main-tier performers were oil company Astra, textile firm and shoemaker Alpargatas and gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, which added 2.2 percent, 1.6 percent and 0.8 percent, respectively.
